symptom: a broad flat hand with too many fingers and no thumb in a young child
hook: the hand had seven fingers arranged like a mirror image of itself
whatYouSee: The hand carries seven fingers laid out like a reflection with no thumb at all and the forearm below it holds two matching bones instead of a radius and an ulna.
whyItMatters: The limb bud duplicated its ulnar half during development so the child has no thumb and no true grip and the elbow is stiff.
treatment: Surgery removes the surplus rays and rebuilds one of them into a thumb so the hand can pinch and grip.
takeaway: A mirrored hand with no thumb over two ulnae is ulnar dimelia.
